q: Did games with smaller crowds coincide with smaller national TV audiences in 2025 and 2026?
title: MLB attendance and national TV audience correlation, 2025-2026
cited: Yes, games with smaller crowds tended to have smaller national TV audiences, but a crowd that was small for its own park did not clearly mean a smaller audience (table: crowd_tv_headline). Comparing games on the same network, the two moved together (correlation 0.34 in 2025, n = 82, range 0.14 to 0.52; 0.47 in 2026, n = 83, range 0.29 to 0.62) (table: crowd_tv_headline). After comparing each game with its own park's usual crowd, the link mostly disappears (0.16 in 2025, range -0.05 to 0.37; 0.14 in 2026, range -0.08 to 0.34; both ranges include zero) (table: crowd_tv_headline). Across team-seasons, teams with higher average home attendance also tended to have larger average national TV audiences (correlation 0.51, n = 56, range 0.29 to 0.68) (table: team_crowd_tv). This is consistent with team-level factors such as popularity and market size, but the data does not show that one causes the other.

q: Why did the Mets over-perform on attendance in 2025?
title: Mets attendance drivers, 2025
cited: The New York Mets averaged 39,316 fans a game in 2025, 21.4% above the 32,383 fans their prior two years of crowds, win rate, and market would predict, up 33.3% from 29,485 fans the season before, and part of this may be a rebound from 18.6% below prediction (table: team_season_model; query: Q2). This surge coincided with the offseason signing of outfielder Juan Soto to a 15-year, $765 million contract ([2025 New York Mets season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_York_Mets_season)). The team also opened the season with a 45–24 record through June 12 ([2025 New York Mets season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_York_Mets_season)), and retired former captain David Wright's number 5 during a pre-game ceremony on July 19 ([2025 New York Mets season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_York_Mets_season)).

This surge coincided with the offseason signing of outfielder Juan Soto to a 15-year, $765 million contract[2]. q: Which network had the biggest national TV audiences in 2026?
title: National TV audiences by network, 2026
cited: Fox had the biggest national TV audiences in the 2026 season among networks with known audiences, narrowly leading Netflix and NBC (table: network_audience). Fox averaged `2,343,875 viewers` across 24 windows with known audiences in 2026 (table: network_audience; query: Q1). Netflix followed closely, averaging `2,314,000 viewers` across 2 games with known audiences (table: network_audience), while NBC averaged `2,312,762 viewers` across 21 games (table: network_audience; query: Q1). ABC averaged `1,794,333 viewers` across 3 games (table: network_audience; query: Q1). ESPN averaged `1,126,208 viewers` across 24 games with known audiences, out of 27 total broadcasts (table: network_audience; query: Q1). Rounding out the list, TBS averaged `614,900 viewers` across 10 games with known audiences out of 25 broadcasts (table: network_audience), and FS1 averaged `385,905 viewers` across 21 games with known audiences out of 39 broadcasts (table: network_audience; query: Q1).

q: Did the Red Sox or the Yankees have better season opener attendance in 2024?
title: Red Sox and Yankees season opener attendance, 2024
cited: The New York Yankees drew 47,812 fans to their 2024 home opener, outdrawing the Boston Red Sox by 11,719 fans after Boston drew 36,093 fans (table: games_clean; query: Q4). The Yankees drew 102.7% of listed capacity, which was 7.1 percentage points above the Red Sox at 95.6% of capacity (table: games_clean; query: Q4).

q: Compare the Cubs and White Sox on attendance and national TV audiences in 2025.
title: Cubs and White Sox attendance and TV audience, 2025
cited: The Chicago Cubs outdrew the Chicago White Sox by 1,572,245 fans (table: team_season_model; query: Q7) in total home attendance and held a massive advantage in national television coverage during the 2025 season. The Cubs averaged 37,259 fans (table: team_season_model), drawing 89.9% of capacity (table: games_clean, team_season_model), which was 19,187 fans (table: team_season_model) and 44.9 percentage points (table: games_clean, team_season_model) ahead of the White Sox average of 18,072 fans (table: team_season_model) at 45.0% of capacity (table: games_clean, team_season_model; query: Q6, Q7). On television, the Cubs had 15 (table: team_tv_summary), including 10 (table: team_tv_summary) that averaged 1,126,444 viewers (table: team_tv_summary) with a peak of 2,041,000 viewers (table: team_tv_summary; query: Q2). Meanwhile, the White Sox had no national TV broadcasts in the 2025 data.
report:
The Chicago Cubs outdrew the Chicago White Sox by 1,572,245 fans in total home attendance and held a massive advantage in national television coverage during the 2025 season[1]. The Cubs averaged 37,259 fans, drawing 89.9% of capacity, which was 19,187 fans and 44.9 percentage points ahead of the White Sox average of 18,072 fans at 45.0% of capacity[2][1]. On television, the Cubs had 15, including 10 that averaged 1,126,444 viewers with a peak of 2,041,000 viewers[3]. Meanwhile, the White Sox had no national TV broadcasts in the 2025 data[4].

q: Did Red Sox night games draw bigger crowds than day games in 2026?
title: Red Sox attendance by game time, 2026
cited: Red Sox night games averaged 35,445 fans a game and drew 93.9% of capacity across 47 dates, while day games averaged 34,576 fans a game and drew 91.6% of capacity over 33 dates (table: games_clean; query: Q4). This gave night games a 2.3 percentage points higher fill rate than day games (table: games_clean; query: Q4).
